Problem Statement:
Protocol signature checking broken for classmethod/staticmethod detection

#### Description

Protocol signature compatibility checking is incorrectly handling classmethod and staticmethod decorators, causing valid protocol implementations to be rejected and invalid ones to be accepted.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from typing import Protocol, Any
from typeguard import check_type

class MyProtocol(Protocol):
    @staticmethod
    def my_static_method(x: int, y: str) -> None:
        pass

    @classmethod
    def my_class_method(cls, x: int, y: str) -> None:
        pass

class Foo:
    @classmethod
    def my_static_method(cls, x: int, y: str) -> None:
        pass

    @staticmethod
    def my_class_method(x: int, y: str) -> None:
        pass

# This should fail but doesn't
check_type(Foo(), MyProtocol)
```

Also affects basic protocol method signature validation:

```python
class SimpleProtocol(Protocol):
    def meth(self) -> None:

class SimpleFoo:

check_type(SimpleFoo(), SimpleProtocol)
```

The protocol checker is not properly detecting method signature mismatches and decorator type mismatches between protocol definitions and their implementations.

entries.content: Done. The root cause was a cluster of inverted/garbled conditions in `check_signature_compatible()` in `src/typeguard/_checkers.py`, which broke all protocol method signature validation: `classmethod` descriptors were misclassified as `"instance"` methods (so valid static↔class implementations were rejected and instance-method mismatches with classmethods were missed); the varargs/varkwargs detection used inverted `all(... is not ...)` logic instead of `any(... is ...)`; the positional-argument comparison ran only when the subject *had* varargs (instead of when it didn't), wrongly popped arguments for static methods, and lacked the `None` padding that lets the "too many/too few positional arguments" checks fire; the mandatory-argument, positional-only, argument-name, and keyword-only checks all had inverted conditions (`is not` vs `is`, `in` vs `not in`, swapped parameter kinds). I restored correct mypy-style semantics throughout: proper instance/class/static detection, `any()`-based vararg detection, positional checks that skip the receiver (`self`/`cls`) and compare padded argument lists, and correctly oriented keyword-only checks. The full test suite (475 tests) plus targeted reproduction and edge-case scripts all pass.
